means: The commons' system for coordinating work: it takes work, does it, keeps its journal, and talks with whoever drives it - a person or a machine alike - built on ocoeco.
not: runner (says nothing of coordination, the journal or the leases); lab-agent (a place, not a family); the machine's hands (too narrow: it coordinates people too)

means: oco-agent's own sign of life, sent from its working loop after each healthy turn to a dead man's switch outside the machine, which alerts the author when pulses stop.
not: beat (a driver's sign of presence); heartbeat (used loosely for both); ping (any request)

means: A driver says something to another driver, or to everyone; it is kept in order, and carried to whoever can be reached away from a keyboard.
not: notify (one-way, to a person only); message (says nothing of who speaks); post (a tool's word)

means: Whoever drives work through oco-agent - a person (the author, anyone) or a machine (an AI such as Claude) - holding the driver's lease while working; oco-agent treats them alike.
not: the agent (the system itself); the user (people only, while a driver may be a machine); the AI (machines only)
